kill_argument: The only flag about the return to schooling, h3b_b6_return_positive, rests on m(b0) = min over g of a non-convex HC1 Wald statistic (ivlib.PanelB.profile), and nothing in h3b-subvector checks on the real data that BFGS reached the global minimum; any shortfall raises m(b0), so it can only shrink the robust set and manufacture a 'positive return'. The brute-force check exists only in check-synthetic, on designs without Card's identity exp76 + ed76 = age76 - 6. I attacked this directly: on the Card-structured synthetic file (runs/check-synthetic/synthetic_card.csv) I compared BFGS with a 61-start Nelder-Mead plus nested 301x301 grids at 17 values of b0 (the 2SLS estimate, 0, both reported bounds, +-0.5 to +-1e5); they agree to 1e-8 everywhere, and the profile levels off near 18.8 at large |b0|. Also attacked and held: k and n-k for every specification, HC1 and conventional formulas, the AR V cross term, the AR quadric, the CHR identity, the IF and D = -rho g algebra, the HAR gradient and kron structure, the LIML kappa, the GKMC quadric, GKM19 (3T) interpolation (table identical to notes sec. 4b), verdict targets (9 and 22), and the absence of any real-data run.

findings.text: The primary H3(b) decision depends on PanelB.profile reaching the global minimum over g, but h3b-subvector checks only the stacked HAR against a direct regression (an algebra check), not the minimisation. The 401x401 brute-force comparison runs only in check-synthetic (designs S and WN, around bhat +- 4 SE), whose data lack the exp76 + ed76 = age76 - 6 identity and the exp76/exp762 scale gap of the real data. Under-minimisation biases m(b0) upward and so can only make the set too narrow (anti-conservative), exactly in the direction of a spurious 'return positive'. My own check on the Card-structured synthetic file held (BFGS = alternative minimiser to 1e-8 at 17 b0 values), so this is a residual risk, not a demonstrated error.
findings.evidence: code/h3b_subvector.py lines 79-86 (only check of the robust statistic); code/ivlib.py PanelB.profile lines 780-789; code/test_ivlib.py panel_b_check lines 339-352 (brute force on synthetic designs only)
findings.response: Accepted as residual risk; the results review is asked to check the h3b minimisation against a brute-force grid on the real profile (no code change before the runs).

findings.text: Two in-run checks depart from the approved design.method and the departures are recorded only in runs/NOTES.md (items 2 and 10), not in plan.json design.deviations: (a) design.method says a disagreement with ivmodels above 1e-6 relative in kappa_p or kappa_1 fails the run, but the code fails only at |b0| <= 1 and writes the differences at reported bounds beyond |b0| = 1 as *_outer metrics; (b) design.method asks for the stacked-vs-direct HAR check at 20 random (b0, g), the code uses 20 evenly spaced b0 on [-0.5, 0.8] with g from the start draws. Neither changes an estimate, and the set-level agreement checks (GKMC quadric and (3Q) vs ivmodels to 1e-4) still fail the run at every bound, but T12 requires changes to be entered as deviations. Remedy: add a D3 entry to design.deviations before the h3b-subvector run; no code change needed.
findings.evidence: code/h3b_subvector.py lines 79-84 and 146-181; plan.json design.method ('a disagreement above 1e-6 relative in the statistic ... fails the run'; '20 random (b0, g)'); plan.json design.deviations (D1, D2 only)
findings.response: Fixed by the PI: recorded as deviation D3 in plan.json design.deviations before any analysis run.

findings.text: Two scripts execute local modules that analysis_plan does not list as their code: h1_a5.py imports panel_a from h1_a6.py, and verdict.py imports ivlib.py. analysis_plan step 3 names 'code/h1_a5.py + ivlib.py' and step 11 names only 'code/verdict.py'. If the runs are launched with those --code lists, the ledger will not hash h1_a6.py for h1-a5 or ivlib.py for verdict, so a later change to them would not invalidate those runs or the code-review coverage check. Remedy: pass --code code/h1_a6.py to h1-a5 and --code code/ivlib.py to verdict (and generally every local module a script imports); no code change needed.
findings.evidence: code/h1_a5.py line 24; code/verdict.py line 25; plan.json design.analysis_plan steps 3 and 11
findings.response: Fixed in the run commands: h1-a5 names code/h1_a6.py and verdict names code/ivlib.py with --code.

findings.text: Finite bounds of non-convex sets are written only as strings, so the paper could not quote them through macros (protocol 0.2) and the figure would label them inexactly. h2h3_weakiv.py writes a6/a5_ar_lo and _hi as the outermost ends (null for a union of two half-lines) and the finite inner bounds only in the a6/a5_ar_pieces string; h3b_subvector.py writes numeric metrics only for the lowest lower bound and the highest upper bound of each set. fig_chr.py piece_ends draws and annotates interior piece ends at grid points rather than the bisected bounds (off by up to the outer-grid spacing, about 3% of |b0| beyond 1). Harmless if every realised set is one bounded interval; if any set is two half-lines or multi-piece, write each piece's bounds as numeric metrics (e.g. *_piece1_lo) and have fig_chr read them before the results gate.
findings.evidence: code/h2h3_weakiv.py lines 50-53; code/h3b_subvector.py lines 114-120; code/fig_chr.py lines 250-255 and 385-394
findings.response: Deferred as the finding allows: applies only if a set is not a single bounded interval; checked at the results review before the results gate.

reviewer_checks_run: Synthetic data only (no real outcome read): in scratch, BFGS profile vs 61-start Nelder-Mead + nested 301x301 grids on runs/check-synthetic/synthetic_card.csv at 17 b0 values (max relative difference < 1e-8 apart from the zero at the 2SLS estimate); ivmodels inverse boundaries on the same file have zero imaginary parts; ivlib GKM19 table equals sources/notes.md sec. 4b (36 rows). Hashes of all 14 code files equal those recorded by check-synthetic.
